experience.description:
During my time as a Junior and FullStack Developer, I participated in the development of TERREC, an application intended for AMTEGA for parcel management at the Galician level. The objective was to unify the management of model villages, agroforestry polygons, ownership investigations, etc., into a single application. Management includes viewing and modifying maps via layers and GIS services.

Regarding technologies, Spring Boot with an Oracle SQL database was used for the backend, and jQuery/JavaScript for the frontend, utilizing ArcGIS for GIS control. Additionally, autonomous deployments were carried out in Jenkins, and JUnit was used for testing. SVN was used for version control.

Integrations with other APIs were also implemented in this application, such as Cadastre, ARPAD, Notifica.gal, PortaSinaturas, and the Xunta's Electronic Office.

Upon transitioning to Technical Lead, I assumed technical direction of two projects: TERREC and XALEA, an inherited project resulting from winning a public tender. The latter manages the distribution of LEADER grants within Rural Development Groups alongside Agader. In addition to all the points touched upon in TERREC, I emphasize the evolution in this project toward best practices, risk analysis, task management within the team, and multiple client meetings aimed at gathering data for application development.

The project I collaborated on is called INQUI, responsible for monitoring IT processes (such as HIS – Hospital Information System, LIS – Laboratory Information System, etc.) in Quirón Salud hospitals.

This allowed me to familiarize myself with the Mirth Connect environment and HL7 messaging in a healthcare setting. My tasks were focused on the backend, also managing a MySQL database. Agile and Scrum methodologies were used for software engineering.
